punchline: When food is scarce, a cell stops growing and starts recycling its own parts.
thirty_sec: Sinclair describes two enzymes. TOR drives growth when food is plentiful; in lean times it holds growth back and cells recycle their parts. AMPK responds to low energy. Eating less animal protein lowers mTOR, and the drug rapamycin did the same in mice, adding 9 to 14 percent to lifespan with a weaker immune response. Critics question parts of his diet advice.
